text: Now three more components, one at a time, starting with cholesterol. In animal cell surface membranes, cholesterol molecules sit among the phospholipids in both layers. Each has a small polar O H group, a hydroxyl group, at one end, and a rigid ring structure that is non-polar. The O H group sits level with the phospholipid heads, towards the water, while the rings lie among the tails in the hydrophobic core. It's the same logic again: the polar part with the polar heads and the water, the non-polar part with the non-polar tails.
